recentItems.title: He was 5 when he found his mom murdered. DNA named her killer 50 years later
recentItems.description:
When Eric Waldman was just five years old, he came home from kindergarten and found his mother, Barbara Waldman, murdered in their Oceanside home on Long Island. Despite witness descriptions and investigative leads, the case remained unsolved for more than five decades. In 2023, renewed efforts and advances in DNA testing and genealogy led investigators to a suspect, Thomas Generazio, who had died years earlier. Now Barbara’s children hope their family's long search for answers inspires others never to give up on seeking justice.

recentItems.title: New York drops Regents exam graduation requirement
recentItems.description:
Beginning with the Class of 2028, New York students will no longer be required to pass a set of Regents exams to graduate. The Board of Regents says the tests will remain an important measure of academic achievement and one of several ways students can demonstrate proficiency. Supporters say the change will reduce pressure on students, while critics worry it lowers academic standards.

recentItems.title: Why homes on Long Island are getting multiple offers so fast
recentItems.description:
Long Island has been named the top seller’s housing market in the nation, according to a Redfin study. Buyers outnumber sellers by 36%, creating intense competition and multiple offers on properly priced homes. Redfin says strong demand, limited inventory, and families pooling resources to buy together are helping keep the market moving.

recentItems.title: Connecticut News Today: Former state official flees to Greece, adult abduction case
recentItems.description:
Several major stories are developing across Connecticut. Nineteen-year-old Deng Deng has returned to the state after being released from immigration detention following his arrest at Tweed New Haven Airport. Testimony has begun in the trial of former Stamford officer Zachary Lockwood, who is accused of criminal negligence in the 2023 death of Reverend Tommie Jackson. Bridgeport police are seeking help identifying a woman linked to a possible adult abduction captured on a Ring doorbell camera. Meanwhile, former state budget deputy Kosta Diamantis is the subject of an international manhunt after authorities say he fled to Greece before sentencing on bribery convictions, and a new report claims Connecticut's college and university system failed to properly handle sexual harassment allegations against former interim chancellor John Maduko.

recentItems.title: Bronx News Today: Pharmacy thefts, DWI arrest and hit-and-run probe
recentItems.description:

Police are searching for four people accused of stealing more than $60,000 in medication and cash during a series of break-ins targeting pharmacies and businesses in the Bronx, Brooklyn and Queens. Exclusive surveillance video shows a woman being struck by a vehicle in Soundview, where police say a person was arrested for driving while intoxicated. Authorities are also investigating a hit-and-run that seriously injured a cyclist in the South Bronx, while the city launches its new “Know Your Zone” campaign to encourage residents to prepare evacuation plans for severe weather events.

recentItems.title: Accused bathroom voyeur found in the Bronx after Norwalk City Hall bathroom recording
recentItems.description:
A woman told police that a man held a cellphone underneath a bathroom stall and appeared to be recording inside Norwalk City Hall. Detectives say surveillance footage helped identify 31-year-old Terrill Kelly as the suspect after he allegedly fled the area. Police later located Kelly in the Bronx and extradited him from Rikers Island back to Norwalk. Authorities say he is being held on a $50,000 bond and is due back in court on Sept. 29.

recentItems.title: Daughter speaks after 2 arrested in mother’s hit-and-run death
recentItems.description:

Investigators say Jahmeir Tillery and Ti Norfleet moved Harris while she was critically injured and failed to get her emergency medical care. Harris’ daughter says she is grateful arrests have finally been made and that justice is being served.

recentItems.title: The untold story behind an iconic Billy Joel 9/11 photo
recentItems.description:
One of the most memorable images from the days after 9/11 showed an FDNY helmet resting on Billy Joel’s piano during the America: A Tribute to Heroes concert. Photographer Kevin Mazur captured the historic moment but spent years wondering who the helmet belonged to. Two decades later, he finally met retired FDNY Lieutenant Neil Skow, the firefighter whose helmet became a symbol of sacrifice, remembrance, and dedication. Their reunion led to a touching recreation of the iconic image with Billy Joel at Madison Square Garden.
